title: Kernel Sandbox — Network Partition Detection and Mitigation Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines detection, containment, and recovery procedures for network partitions that affect kernel sandboxes (in-process kernel plugins, accelerator-sidecar communication, and scheduler control plane paths). It focuses on protecting SLOs and KV-cache consistency while minimizing blast radius during transient or prolonged network disruptions.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to nodes running the runtime kernel sandbox (kernel sidecar, kernel plugin process, and LocalScheduler agent).
- Covers partitions that break control-plane RPCs (gRPC/HTTP/QUIC) between: LocalScheduler <-> KernelSidecar, KernelSidecar <-> KVCacheShard, and NodeAgent <-> ControlPlane.
- Does NOT replace general cluster-network runbooks (CNI, cloud-provider network faults). Use in conjunction with eng-infra networking runbooks.

Goals / SLO impact:
- Preserve 99th percentile tail latency SLOs where possible by isolating affected cohorts.
- Prevent KV-cache corruption or inconsistent warmstart data across shards.
- Avoid unsafe kernel-handoff operations during partition.

Ownership:
- Primary: serving-runtime-kernel (oncall rotation)
- Escalation: eng-sre (if >30m or cross-region impact)
- Communications: incident commander from eng-sre for P1s

Detection and automated triggers (observability):
1) Short signals (automated):
  - kernel_sidecar_rpc_failures_total > 5/min for a node for 3 consecutive minutes
  - kvcache_replica_sync_lag_seconds > 10s for a shard
  - scheduler-heartbeat-missed_count >= 3 for a LocalScheduler agent
2) Composite trigger (higher confidence):
  - (rpc_failures AND heartbeat_missed) OR (packet_loss_node_percent > 3% AND request_tail_99_latency > baseline + 40ms)

Prometheus queries to surface on Ops dashboard (copy into alert & pager rules):
- alert: KernelSidecarRPCsHighFailureRate
  expr: increase(kernel_sidecar_rpc_failures_total[3m]) > 5
- alert: KVCacheReplicaLag
  expr: max_over_time(kvcache_replica_sync_lag_seconds[5m]) > 10
- useful ad-hoc query:
  sum by(node) (increase(kernel_sidecar_rpc_failures_total[5m])) / sum by(node) (increase(kernel_sidecar_rpc_requests_total[5m]))

Immediate containment (automated actions recommended):
- Mark node as degraded in RuntimeClusterState to prevent new warmstarts: POST /runtime-admin/nodes/{node}/degrade (example tool below).
- Fallback routing: route new requests from that node’s router to cross-region fallback pools if latency budget allows.
- Disable cross-node KV-cache writes for affected shards (set kvcache.shard.<id>.write_enabled = false) to prevent split-brain writes.

Runbook: step-by-step manual procedure
1) Triage (5–10 min)
   - Confirm alert: check Prometheus graphs and query the three signals above.
   - Identify scope: run `rtctl node list --filter=node=<node>` and `rtctl shard status --node <node>` to list affected kernels and shards.
   - Check node-level networking: `kubectl -n runtime get pod -o wide | grep <node>` and `kubectl exec -it <kernel-sidecar-pod> -- ss -tunap` to inspect connections.
2) Short-term containment (10–30 min)
   - Run: `rtctl node annotate <node> degraded=network-partition --owner=<your-name>` (prevents automated warmstart scheduling).
   - Disable KV-cache writes for shards with lag: `rtctl kvcache set <shard-id> write_enabled=false --reason=\"partition\"`
   - Trigger immediate fallback policy: `rtctl routing force-fallback --node <node>`
3) Recovery actions (30–120 min)
   - If partition appears to be due to node-local firewall/CNI, coordinate with infra: collect `tcpdump` from node and kernel-sidecar namespace: `kubectl exec -it <sidecar> -- tcpdump -i any -w /tmp/partition.pcap` then collect.
   - For control-plane partitions, consider temporarily enabling control-plane proxying: `kubectl apply -f /configs/controlplane-proxy-nginx.yaml` (see Appendix).
   - When connectivity restored, re-enable writes and warmstarts in this order per shard: re-enable writes -> warm cache with staff-initiated replay -> monitor kvcache_replica_sync_lag_seconds until <1s for 5m -> remove node degraded annotation.
4) Validation and monitoring (post-recovery, next 60 min)
   - Watch key metrics: request_tail_99_latency, kernel_sidecar_rpc_failures_total, kvcache_replica_sync_lag_seconds.
   - Run a synthetic traffic replay against the affected node’s pods: `loadgen --target=<node-pod-ip> --profile=warm-path-10pps --duration=2m` and validate fidelity.

Automated remediation tool snippets
- Degrade node (example curl):
  curl -X POST https://runtime-admin.internal/api/v1/nodes/<node>/degrade -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN\" -d '{\"reason\":\"network-partition-detected\",\"owner\":\"oncall\"}'
- Toggle kvcache writes (example JSON payload):
  {"shard_id":"shard-23","write_enabled":false,"reason":"partition-isolation"}

Config table: recommended thresholds and enforcement actions
| Signal | Threshold | Automated action | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| kernel_sidecar_rpc_failures_total (per node) | >5 in 3m | Mark node degraded, fallback routing | serving-runtime-kernel |
| kvcache_replica_sync_lag_seconds (per shard) | >10s | Disable writes | serving-runtime-kernel |
| scheduler-heartbeat-missed_count | >=3 | Pause new warmstarts | eng-sre |

Edge cases and safety notes:
- If a node is in a partial partition (can reach control-plane but not specific KV shard), do NOT perform global cache clears—only isolate affected shards.
- Avoid immediate orchestrated kernel handoffs while any kvcache write-disabled flag is set. Handoffs should be performed only when `kvcache_replica_sync_lag_seconds < 1s`.
- For prolonged partitions (>90m), escalate to eng-sre to consider pod eviction and reprovisioning if the node cannot reliably recover.

Testing and rollout guidance:
1) Unit test: simulate rpc failure by toggling an iptables rule in the kernel-sidecar test harness. Verify node enters degraded state and fallback routing occurs.
2) Stage rollout (canary): enable auto-degrade-on-failure for 5% of nodes in the canary pool for 2 weeks. Collect false-positive rate and recovery windows.
3) Pre-merge checklist for changes to auto-degrade logic: code-level unit tests, integration test against synthetic partition harness, and SLO regression run.

Post-incident analysis template (to fill after incident):
- Incident start/end times:
- Affected nodes / shards:
- Root cause hypothesis:
- Containment actions taken and timeline:
- Recovery steps and time-to-repair:
- Post-mortem action items (owner + due date):
  1) Improve alert sensitivity threshold (owner: )
  2) Add automated pcap collection (owner: )
  3) Runbook clarifications (owner: )

Appendix: useful snippets and configs
- controlplane-proxy-nginx.yaml (short):
  apiVersion: apps/v1
  kind: Deployment
  metadata:
    name: controlplane-proxy
    namespace: runtime-admin
  spec:
    replicas: 2
    template:
      spec:
        containers:
        - name: nginx-proxy
          image: nginx:stable
          ports:
          - containerPort: 8080
          volumeMounts: []

- Observability playbook additions (Grafana panels to add):
  - Per-node RPC failure heatmap (3m window)
  - KV-cache sync lag by shard (5m moving max)
  - Node degraded annotation overlay on request latency charts
